records.name_as_stated: Portafolio de Inversion Administrado por Banco Mundial (BM)
records.detail: Nota 4.2 'Portafolio de Inversiones Neto' of the Banco Central de Honduras audited financial statements at 31 December 2024 carries a line 'Portafolio de Inversion Administrado por Banco Mundial' of L26,691,806,174 (L24,920,989,813 at 31 December 2023), inside a net foreign investment portfolio of L133,385,068,726 against total reserve assets of L202,903,343,593; the auditor's Key Audit Matter 1 'Reservas Internacionales' says part of the portfolio is managed 'de forma externa a traves de instituciones internacionales especializadas en gestion de portafolios'. The statements name no custodian and no commercial manager.
records.source_title: Banco Central de Honduras, Estados Financieros y Opinion de los Auditores Independientes, 31 de diciembre de 2024 (auditor Horwath Central America, S. de R.L. de C.V., 19 March 2025), Key Audit Matter 'Reservas Internacionales' and Nota 4.2
records.quote: Portafolio de Inversion Administrado por Banco Mundial (BM).

records.name_as_stated: Portafolio de Inversion Administrado por Banco Interamericano de Desarrollo (BID)
records.detail: The same Nota 4.2 of the Banco Central de Honduras audited financial statements at 31 December 2024 carries a line 'Portafolio de Inversion Administrado por Banco Interamericano de Desarrollo' of L5,384,987,889 (L5,013,156,345 at 31 December 2023), beside the World Bank-administered portfolio and a third line for the portfolio the Banco Central de Honduras administers itself (L69,006,363,182). The auditor's Key Audit Matter on international reserves describes this part of the reserves as managed externally through international institutions specialised in portfolio management.

records.quote: Portafolio de Inversion Administrado por Banco Interamericano de Desarrollo (BID).

records.name_as_stated: a green investment fund set up and managed by the Bank for International Settlements
records.detail: The Annual Accounts of the Banco de Espana 2025, opened for the first time this round, state in the note on claims on non-euro area residents denominated in foreign currency that the 'Other' item includes holdings in a US dollar-denominated green investment fund 'set up and managed by the Bank for International Settlements' with a market value of EUR 93.55 million, and in the note on claims on non-euro area residents denominated in euro that the item includes holdings in a green investment fund set up and managed by the BIS with a market value of EUR 382.12 million (EUR 374.34 million in 2024), both as at 31 December 2025. The accounts name no commercial external manager.
records.source_title: Annual Accounts of the Banco de Espana 2025, notes on claims on non-euro area residents denominated in foreign currency and denominated in euro
records.quote: holdings in a US dollar-denominated green investment fund set up and managed by the Bank for International Settlements

blanks.note: The document r69 could not reach was opened. Route that worked: the section page https://www.bde.es/bde/en/secciones/informes/informes-y-memorias-anuales/cuentas-anuales/ serves to plain curl (200, 421 KB) and lists every year's PDF; the repositorio handle 123456789/39439 returns 403 and is dead. Annual Accounts of the Banco de Espana 2025 (https://www.bde.es/f/webbe/SES/Secciones/Publicaciones/PublicacionesAnuales/Cuentas_anuales_del_BdE/2025/files/CuentasAnuales_2025_Ing.pdf, 2.2 MB, 155,856 characters) downloaded and grepped in full: zero hits for 'external manager', 'externally managed', 'mandates awarded', 'RAMP', 'IBRD', 'World Bank', 'BlackRock', 'Amundi', 'PIMCO', 'UBS', 'Wellington', 'Crown Agents', 'ETF'. The only outside manager anywhere in the accounts is the BIS, which is filed as a record. The accounting-policy note 'Shares in marketable investment funds' sets out the criteria for recording fund units (acquired 'with no influence on the fund's day-to-day buy and sell decisions', the fund 'managed independently') but names no fund and no manager. So: no commercial external manager of Spanish reserves in the audited accounts. Untried residual vein: Plataforma de Contratacion del Sector Publico award notices for Banco de Espana asset-management mandates.

Reached this round. Route: https://www.nbb.be/en/publications-and-research/annual-reports (200) -> https://www.nbb.be/en/publications-research/publications/corporate-report -> https://www.nbb.be/en/publications-research/all-publications/report-2025-corporate-report, which gives working paths report2025_t2.pdf and three part files (the t2_2022_complet path r69 tried is genuinely gone). National Bank of Belgium Corporate Report 2025 (https://www.nbb.be/doc/ts/publications/nbbreport/2025/en/t2/report2025_t2.pdf, 9.5 MB, 560,053 characters) downloaded and grepped in full: zero hits for 'external manager', 'externally managed', 'gestionnaire', 'vermogensbeheer', 'mandates awarded', 'RAMP', 'World Bank', 'IBRD', 'BlackRock', 'Amundi', 'PIMCO', 'UBS', 'Wellington', 'Crown Agents', 'BISIP', 'outsourc' (one hit, in an operational-risk list). The relevant passage is in section 3.1.2.1 on the Bank's own portfolios: the Bank 'invests a portion of its own investment portfolios in dollar-denominated corporate bonds and a limited share in a dedicated investment fund... composed of shares of European companies that reflect as closely as possible the performance of a European index, excluding the United Kingdom and Switzerland. The fund is managed externally and passively so as to avoid conflicts of interest.' That states external management but names NO manager, so there is nothing to file; the only figure attached is the 'Investment funds' line of the euro-denominated securities portfolio, EUR 1,516.6 million at end-2025 (EUR 1,265.3 million at end-2024). A named-manager record for Belgium therefore has to come from somewhere else: the untried vein is publicprocurement.be award notices for the NBB equity-fund mandate, which that passage shows exists.

Reached this round on the Ministry of Finance side, where Japan's reserves sit (Foreign Exchange Fund Special Account, FEFSA). The FEFSA index https://www.mof.go.jp/policy/international_policy/gaitame_kawase/foreign_exchange_fund_special_account/index.html lists exactly the two pages that would name a manager, and both were opened by plain curl. (1) 'Registration relating to the external delegation of foreign currency assets held in the FEFSA' (gaitame_emanager.htm) says that following the amendment of the Special Accounts Act outside management of FEFSA assets became possible from April 2014, that MOF accepts standing registrations of candidate managers for its foreign bonds under Article 76(6), that applicants must be trust companies or registered investment managers with at least five years' foreign-bond experience and at least JPY 300 billion of foreign bonds under management, and that MOF selects from the register 'as necessary' and contacts firms itself. It names NOT ONE firm - a mechanism, not a record. (2) gaitametokkai_170404_rev.html sets out the investment objective, principles, eligible assets and risk management, and its counterparty section says only that counterparties for deposits, bond purchases and sales, FX swaps, bond lending and bond deposits are selected on ratings, financial condition, market record and administrative capacity - again no names, and the brief's rule puts a counterparty list outside this row anyway. Residual vein: the FEFSA settlement statements / disclosure pages under mof.go.jp/about_mof/mof_budget/special_account/gaitame/ and reference/gaitametokkai/, and a disclosure request for the register itself; also the Bank of Japan's own (much smaller) foreign assets in the BOJ Annual Review.
